# Part X. Behavior and Decision Design {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note .part-overview icon=false}
## Why this part comes last

Knowledge is not implementation. Earlier parts explained why attention, probability, risk, time, habit, social meaning, communication, and power bend behavior. The book ends by using that full diagnosis to design feasible actions, choice environments, and decision systems without making the chooser disappear.
:::

## Guiding questions

- What ability, motivation, prompt, friction, or default should change?
- Which earlier mechanism is the intervention trying to change?
- How can the decision system preserve independence, learn, and remain accountable?
- Would the design remain defensible if the people affected understood how it worked?

## Closing the loop

The book returns to its first claim: visible action is only the tip of the iceberg. We can now inspect—and ethically redesign—the attention, models, probabilities, reference points, social processes, environments, and feedback beneath it.
